title: Financial Counseling Schedule: Balance Ceiling on a Re-aged Patient Payment Plan
content:
The longest re-aged schedule of a **Patient Payment Plan** may run past the tier's maximum term only as far as the balance ceiling of the re-aged schedule allows, following Riverbend's term schedule by balance read from the plan's own ledger as the amounts enrolled less the installments paid (the down payment included) and the reductions booked.

**Rule.** 60 installments when that balance is at least 10000.00 and 48 installments when it is at least 3000.00, the first of these that applies, each only on tiers whose maximum term is shorter; otherwise the balance ceiling is the tier's maximum term.

| Tier | Tier maximum term | Ledger balance at least 10000.00 | At least 3000.00, below 10000.00 | Below 3000.00 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riverbend Short-Term Payment Plan | 6 | 60 | 48 | 6 |
| Riverbend Standard Payment Plan | 12 | 60 | 48 | 12 |
| Riverbend Extended Payment Plan | 24 | 60 | 48 | 24 |
| Riverbend Long-Term Payment Plan | 36 | 60 | 48 | 36 |
| Riverbend Assistance-Linked Payment Plan | 48 | 60 | 48 | 48 |
| Riverbend Hardship Payment Plan | 60 | 60 | 60 | 60 |

**Hypothetical.** Enrolled 4000.00, paid 800.00, reductions 0.00: the ledger balance is 3200.00, so a plan of a tier with a 24-installment maximum term has a balance ceiling of 48. Had 1300.00 been paid, the balance of 2700.00 would leave the ceiling at 24.
